solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Platonic attachment of Nero, say, in pre-Christian time

indicators.note: the emperor's nationality sits inside the era abbreviation

parts.note: BCE, Before Common Era, marks dates before Christ
Nero was a Roman emperor, so an example of a Roman

explanation.surface: A historian notes an emperor's close friendship in the years before Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: A close but non-sexual friendship between two men is the modern slang sense of the word.

clue.text: Refrain from, as the French say, splitting stream

indicators.note: the French word cuts the watercourse in two, sitting in its middle

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream
de is French for from

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep away from a stream, as the French would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning abstain, but it is the noun: the repeated chorus of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A song's chorus or recurring theme is an older sense of the word, as in the burden of a ballad.

clue.text: America's film industry would cover this Spanish city in 2000

indicators.note: the industry word is the city wrapped in the Roman numeral, so removing that wrapping leaves the city

parts.note: moviedom is the world of American movies
MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Hollywood might have covered a Spanish city on film at the millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would cover this ... in 2000' says the industry word is this city held inside MM, the Roman 2000; take the outer M and M away.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Psychiatrist who causes confusion when missing a day

indicators.note: one letter for a day is absent from the word for a confuser

parts.note: an addler is someone who muddles or confuses
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is described as a confuser who goes absent for a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was the Austrian psychiatrist who founded individual psychology.

clue.text: Staff in centre deteriorate

indicators.note: the staff word is placed within the middle word

parts.note: a core is the centre of something
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees at the heart of an organisation are going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to wear away gradually, which is to deteriorate.

clue.text: Chanteuse fine to eat large spicy dish

indicators.note: the singer and the fine letter take in the large letter, swallowing it

parts.note: Edith Piaf was the famous French chanteuse
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A singer is happy to eat a big spicy dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is rice cooked in stock with spices, a Middle Eastern and Indian dish.

clue.text: First hot month on river

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hot
Aug is the abbreviation for August
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: The first hot month arrives on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the first of its kind, the one that opens a series.

clue.text: First off, relatives must catch taxi without fighting

indicators.note: the trimmed relatives word takes the taxi inside it
the opening letter of the relatives word is dropped

parts.note: family means one's relatives
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Relatives must hail a taxi first, before any squabbling starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a friendly, peaceable way means there is no quarrel.

clue.text: Leading positions go in management of large plants

parts.note: fores are front positions, as in to the fore
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Top jobs are on offer in the management of big industrial plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large plants' suggests factories; here they are trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending woodland, the cultivation of trees, is a fair description of managing big plants.

clue.text: Skate around apparently less healthy banter

indicators.note: the fish goes round the comparative word

parts.note: a skate is a kind of ray
iller would be the comparative of ill, apparently because it is rarely used

explanation.surface: A skater going round looks less well, prompting teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, the same as banter.

clue.text: Cross connected with a rival saint

parts.note: X is a cross shape
a vier is one who vies, a rival

explanation.surface: An angry person is linked with a rival saint.
explanation.definitionFit: St Francis Xavier was the Jesuit missionary to Asia.

clue.text: Recognise deficient bishop as boss

indicators.note: the recognise word lacks its final letter

parts.note: to know is to recognise
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone fails to identify the bishop as their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer, but it is a raised stud or knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round protuberance, such as an ornamental stud or handle.

clue.text: One weird tip for duvet, shaking its cover

indicators.note: the letters are shaken about into a new order
the tip of the word duvet is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An odd tip for keeping a duvet fluffy: shake its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaking' rearranges ONE WEIRD plus D. 'Its cover' refers back to the sea duck behind the name: the soft plumage that covers it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine breast feathers of the eider duck are its covering, used to stuff quilts.

clue.text: Composer of arpeggios for flute, for one

definitions.meaning: Philip ..., the American minimalist whose music is built on repeated arpeggios
a flute is a tall narrow drinking vessel for champagne

explanation.surface: A composer writes arpeggios for the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Glass is the minimalist composer, and a champagne flute is a drinking vessel made of that material.

clue.text: Sentimentally pretty wife wearing casual top

indicators.note: the wife letter is inside the shirt, as if wearing it

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A wife in a T-shirt looks sweet and sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee, a British word, means affectedly quaint or sugary-cute.

clue.text: After marriage vow, with husband buried in box, perhaps, the state one's in?

indicators.note: the vow, the with letter and the husband letter are sunk inside the timber word

parts.note: box is a kind of wood
I do is the vow said at a wedding

explanation.surface: After the wedding vows, the husband lies dead in a coffin: what does that make the bride?
explanation.walkthrough: The box is a coffin in the story, but in the wordplay it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died and been buried is in the condition of a widow.

clue.text: Food returned, mostly fat, for a nicker

indicators.note: the food word is sent back, read the other way

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: most of the fat word, its last letter gone

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Food comes back, mostly greasy, in return for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicker' looks like slang for a pound sterling; here it is one who nicks, British slang for steals.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who breaks in to steal is someone who nicks things.

clue.text: Sister to decline white robe after raising yaks

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the pieces makes them read bottom to top

parts.note: to ebb is to decline
an alb is a white vestment worn by priests

explanation.surface: A nun turns down a white habit after rearing yaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yaks' are the animals in the story, but the definition is the verb: chatters.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to talk incessantly, which is to chatter on foolishly.

clue.text: Bird losing energy to massage topless house keeper

indicators.note: the bird gives up its energy letter
the energy letter goes in exchange to the trimmed massage word

parts.note: a pelican is a large water bird
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the massage word loses its top letter

parts.note: to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: A bird loses energy to a topless massage given by a housekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House keeper' looks like a domestic servant, but the house is a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord who runs a British pub, a public house, keeps that house.

clue.text: Hollywood location covered by scrub?

parts.note: Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles
under means covered by

explanation.surface: A Hollywood spot is hidden by brushwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrub' looks like a noun for bushes; the question mark flags the verb, to wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash clothes is to clean them by scrubbing, the laundry sense.

clue.text: Start of high growth with grassy leaves

definitions.meaning: the sudden surge felt when a drug takes effect
a marsh plant with long grass-like stems

explanation.surface: A high begins with grassy growth.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of a drug's euphoria is a surge of feeling, and the marsh plant used for chair seats has grassy stems.

clue.text: Pet rock finally discarded by creep

indicators.note: the creep word throws away the closing letter of rock

parts.note: to skulk is to creep about furtively

indicators.note: the final letter of the word rock

explanation.surface: A pet rock is thrown out by a nasty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' reads as a tame animal, but it means a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pet is to be in a huff, which is a mood of brooding resentment.

clue.text: Great cathedral let sacristan put up screens

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up makes the letters read upwards
the words hide the letters behind them, as a screen does

explanation.surface: A great cathedral allows the sacristan to erect screens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screens' hides RALLETS in 'cathedral let sacristan', and 'put up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar, literally of the stars, also means outstanding or excellent.

clue.text: Jokingly seeing son is about to shoot up

indicators.note: the son letter is seen giving way to the about letter

parts.note: in jest means jokingly
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Seeing their son about to inject drugs, a parent treats it as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'son is about' says S becomes C, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To inject a drug is to shoot up in drug slang.

clue.text: US president shortly to receive a shock

indicators.note: the shortened president takes the A inside
the president's name cut short, last letter gone

parts.note: Harry Truman was a US president

explanation.surface: A US president is about to get a nasty shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: British Liberal blocks deviating regulation

indicators.note: the Liberal letter sits in the deviating word, blocking it

parts.note: to yaw is to deviate from a course

explanation.surface: A British Liberal obstructs a wayward regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A local rule made by a council is a regulation with legal force.

clue.text: Second small banknote, note extracted for bribe

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: one note letter is pulled out of the banknote word

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note
N is one of the musical notes in solfa-free crossword usage, here simply a letter called a note

explanation.surface: A second small banknote, with one note taken out, is offered as a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe offered to win someone over.

clue.text: Bargain basement's bottom heap

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bottom of the word is its last letter

parts.note: a ruck is a heap or pile

explanation.surface: The bargain basement's bottom shelf is a jumbled heap.
explanation.definitionFit: To truck is to barter or deal, as in having no truck with someone.

clue.text: Third-party safekeeping for goods in key dispute

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: A third party holds goods while a key dispute is resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit held by an independent party until conditions are met is the legal arrangement meant.

clue.text: Copper nabbing unpleasant person with a bumbling detective

indicators.note: the copper symbol grabs the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a louse is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests a nasty character alongside a clumsy detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Clouseau is the inept French detective of the Pink Panther films.

clue.text: Clerical bodies pronounce agreements, ignoring answer

indicators.note: the answer letter is left out

parts.note: to say is to pronounce
nods are signs of agreement

explanation.surface: Church councils declare agreements without giving an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Councils of church clergy that govern a denomination are such assemblies.

clue.text: Narrow fissure a trailer reported in volcanic island

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the island

parts.note: a crack is a narrow fissure, and a tower is one who tows, a trailer, so the phrase is crack a tower

explanation.surface: A narrow crack, so a trailer reports, opens up in a volcanic island.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a non-rhotic British accent, CRACK A TOWER sounds like the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakatoa is the Indonesian volcanic island whose 1883 eruption was catastrophic.
